compounding_issues: Session-limit throttling blocked every session: S1 got one prompt turn (read app.py, announced a plan) then was cut off; S2–S5 produced only step_start → 'You've hit your session limit' → step_finish with 0 tokens and ~2s duration each

Seed/codebase mismatch: the seed worktree contains a 260-line Flask Auth API (tier2_small/bad), but the story asks for a WebSocket notification server — the agent's only real action in S1 was exploring an unrelated codebase

The 5 '[story]' commits contain no code changes, only .instrument transcript files, so the commit labels (greenfield → feature_addition → integration → refactor → cross_cutting) describe an arc that never happened
key_decisions: No architectural decisions were made — the agent wrote zero code; the only consequential choice was the experiment harness committing empty instrument-only commits instead of failing the session
The seed selection (Flask Auth API for a notification-service story) was the binding decision, and it was wrong for the task
Session 1's intent to build the WebSocket server with a health endpoint and tests was expressed but never executed
story_review.trajectory_description: Flat at zero. Session 1 was the only session with any agentic activity (a codebase read and a stated plan) before the session limit fired; sessions 2 through 5 were empty placeholders that added no tokens, no files, and no cost. Because nothing was produced, quality neither improved nor degraded — the project never started, and the final tree differs from the seed only by six transcript files. test_count is 0, test_code_ratio is 0.0, and all_successful is False.
story_review.summary: A fully failed run — the session-limit throttling prevented any code from being written across all 5 sessions, leaving an unrelated Flask Auth seed untouched and rendering the commit sequence a sequence of empty placeholders rather than a story.
